{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status" },
  "read": "The customer catch stung their confidence at a deep level — they now see every deliverable as a potential repeat failure. The triple-checking is not laziness or defiance; it is self-protection from another public mistake. Underneath it is a status wound: a customer saw them slip up, which hits the question of whether they actually belong in this role.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Push them to speed back up and stop overthinking — which confirms their fear that you see them as deficient and makes the anxiety worse, not better." },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the sting of the incident plainly, reframe careful review as a skill not a flaw, then work together on a scoped quality check process so they have a reliable system instead of free-floating dread.",
  "holdFirm": ["Delivery pace has to come back to a sustainable baseline — the team depends on it.", "One round of structured review per deliverable is the standard, not open-ended triple-passes."],
  "stayFlexible": ["Let them define the checklist items so they own the process.", "Agree on what level of review each type of task actually warrants rather than applying one-size pressure."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I wanted to grab a few minutes with you. That customer catch was uncomfortable — I get it. Nobody wants their work flagged like that, and I am not going to pretend it felt fine." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I have noticed you are putting a lot more review time into everything since then. Walk me through what is going on in your head when you are checking — what are you worried is going to slip through?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I am thinking: instead of eyeballing everything multiple times and hoping, what if we built you an actual short checklist for the two or three things that tend to go sideways? One pass with a solid system catches more than three anxious passes without one. You know this work better than I do — what would need to be on it?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I want to be straight with you: I need your velocity back, and I am holding you to that because I think you are good at this job — the customer thing was one moment, not a verdict. I have high standards for your output and I am saying that specifically because I believe you can meet them. Let us try the checklist for two weeks and check in on how it feels." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Once velocity stabilizes, point out specific deliverables that cleared cleanly so they build a track record of evidence against the inner critic — over time that replaces the dread with a grounded sense of their own competence."
}
situation: A junior shipped something with a mistake a customer caught, and now they are triple-checking everything and velocity has cratered.
